Output: (a) Interpretation Lock FIRST (one bullet per source line): - Line <ID> <copy exact source line> => Locked Meaning (truth-conditions) - If comparative/degree: define entities A,B, relation (>,<,≈), and degree (e.g., "slightly"). - Note: A>B is equivalent to B<A; do not reverse the ordering. (b) THEN ONE Markdown table consistent with the Lock: - [Source Word] | [Morphology] | [Reference Equivalent] | [Contextual Definition] | [Grammatical Role] Source Text: 94 ché questa bestia, per la qual tu gride, 95 non lascia altrui passar per la sua via, 96 ma tanto lo 'mpedisce che l'uccide; Reference Translation (provided): for this beast, because of which thou criest out, lets not any one pass along her way, but so hinders him that she kills him!

**Interpretation Lock – FIRST**
- **Line 94** *ché questa bestia, per la qual tu gride,* → **Locked Meaning**: There exists a particular beast **b** (the “this beast”) such that the addressee **you** ( *tu* ) cries out (**gride**) because of **b**. In logical form: `CAUSE(b, CRY_OUT(you))` or `because(b, cries_out(you))`.
- **Line 95** *non lascia altrui pasar per la sua via,* → **Locked Meaning**: The beast **b** does **not** permit any other person (**altrui**) to **pass** (**pasar**) along **its** way (**la sua via**). Formally: `¬ALLOW(b, ∀p [person(p) ∧ p ≠ b] → PASS_ALONG(p, way_of(b)))`.
- **Line 96** *ma tanto lo 'mpedisce che l'uccide;* → **Locked Meaning**: The beast **b** **hinders** (**'mpedisce**) the same person **p** (the “him” *lo*) **to such a degree** (**tanto**) that the hindrance **kills** (**l’uccide**) him. Define **A** = intensity of hindrance, **B** = lethal threshold. The relation is **A > B** with the degree expressed by “tanto” ( *so much* ). Formally: `DEGREE(A) > B ∧ HINDER(b, p, A) → KILL(b, p)`.
